question.problem:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is ${a}_{n}=1-9n$ for $n\ge 1.$ The recursive formula for this sequence is

${a}_{n+1}=$
{{field-1}},
$\,{a}_{1}=$
{{field-2}},
$\,n\ge 1.$
question.worked_solution:
The recursive formula for an arithmetic sequence is as follows:

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}+d,\,{a}_{1}=___\,,\,n\ge 1
$$

To complete the formula, we need to work out the first term and common difference. The first two terms are

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =1-9(1)=-8 \\ {a}_{2} & =1-9(2)=-17\end{aligned}
$$

and the common difference is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =-17-(-8) \\  & =-17+8 \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first term is ${a}_{1}=-8$ and the common difference is $d=-9.$ Therefore, the recursive formula is as follows:

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}-9,\,{a}_{1}=-8,\,n\ge 1
$$
